text: When the <highlight>strings</highlight> utility is missing on a target, you can use <highlight>grep</highlight> to extract human-readable text from compiled binaries. This is essential for finding hardcoded paths, hidden commands, or credentials.

title: Flag Breakdown
items: -a : Tells grep to treat the binary file as text (Avoids 'Binary file matches' error).
'[[:print:]]{4,}' : Matches any sequence of printable characters that is 4 or more characters long.

text: Look for system calls. If you see <highlight>/bin/echo</highlight> (Absolute Path), it is secure. If you see just <highlight>date</highlight> (Relative Path), it is vulnerable to $PATH Hijacking.

title: Steps Performed
items: Attempt to run strings on the binary to find system calls
Use the cat + grep workaround if strings is not installed
Search for commands called without absolute paths (e.g., date, ls, cat)
Create a malicious script with the same name in /tmp
Export /tmp to the beginning of the $PATH variable
Execute the SUID binary to trigger the hijack and gain root
